To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the optimum concentration of chiral selector is equal to its reciprocal average binding constant and that selectivity is determined by both enthalpic and entropic contributions.

the enantiomeric separation of tioconazoles in capillary electrophoretic systems is controlled by the concentration of cyclodextrins, and the separation selectivity depends on the thermodynamic properties of the cyclodextrin-azole complexation.

the optimum concentration of cyclodextrins for enantioselective separations in capillary electrophoretic analysis of enantiomers is the concentration of cyclodextins in the free form and that the selectivity in the separations is determined by the thermodynamic parameters of the binding process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a systematic approach for optimization of chiral separations in free-solution capillary electrophoretic systems.
the development of a new method of analysis for enantiomers.
the development of a new approach for optimization of enantioseparations in CE.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
capillary electrophoretic separations of enantiomeres with chiral mobile-phase modifiers can be optimized to yield high selectivity and high efficiency separations.
the selectivity is determined by the relative binding strengths of the two reactant enantiomers, but that the magnitude of the separation depends on the concentration of free cyclodextrin.
the separation of the two tioconazole isomers is a complex phenomenon that is dependent upon the nature of the cyclodextrin, its concentration and the type of alcohol used in the buffer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the selectivity of cyclodextrins is determined by a combination of the binding constants, enthalpy changes and entropy changes for complexation of enantiomeres, and that these can be determined by CE.

the enantiomer separation is determined by the relative strength of binding to the selector, but that the relative binding strengths can be modulated through changes in the nature of the host and guest.

cyclodextrin enantiomeric separation is governed by a complex interplay of host-guest binding constants and selectivities, and that the optimum separation conditions are dictated by the relative concentrations of the enantiomer and selector.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding constants of the analyte to the chiral selector and the selectivity of the separation can be estimated from the electrophoretic mobilities of the enantiomers.
chiral selectors can be optimized in terms of both selectivity and resolution.
chiral selectors can be used to optimize enantiomeric separation in CE, and that binding equilibria between the enantiomeric reactants and the selector are the primary determinant of selectivity.
